test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 11 Oct 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What was the main reason behind Mendel's success in deriving the laws of inheritance?

options.text: He studied only one character at a time in his crosses.
He chose parents that were identical.
He counted the individuals exhibiting a particular trait in each generation.

solution:
The correct answer is __**He studied only one character at a time in his crosses**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Mendel's success was due to his meticulous approach.
 
• He used pea plants (Pisum sativum).
 
• Pea plants are easy to grow.
 
• They have a short generation time.
 
• They produce many offspring.
 
• They have distinct, observable traits.
 
• Pea plants can self-pollinate.
 
• Mendel focused on single traits at a time.
 
• This simplified the analysis of inheritance.
 
• He used pure-breeding lines.
 
• These lines consistently produced offspring with the same trait.
 
• They served as the foundation for his crosses.
 
• Mendel used mathematical analysis.
 
• He recorded the number of offspring with each trait.
 
• He applied statistical analysis to his data.
 
• This allowed him to identify patterns and ratios.
 
• He meticulously kept records.
 
• He documented every step of his experiments.
 
• His detailed records were essential for his analysis.
 
• His experiments were carefully controlled.
 
• This minimized the influence of external factors.
 
• He grew plants in a controlled environment.
 
• He carefully selected plants for his crosses.
 
• This allowed him to attribute inheritance to genetic factors.
 
• He presented his findings clearly and concisely.
